questions.prompt: Describe the five steps of the request loop.
questions.modelAnswer: Capture the request as a ticket on the task board, assign it to yourself or the right team, fulfil it within the service-level target, close the loop by confirming with the guest, then close the ticket with the completion time.
keyPoints: Close the loop with the guest

questions.prompt: What can you approve on your own without the Duty Manager?
questions.modelAnswer: Late checkout up to 1:00 PM, complimentary items under $20, and a room move to the same category when a room is available.

questions.prompt: A ticket with a 30-minute target has been open for an hour. What's the rule?
questions.modelAnswer: At double the target time you personally update the guest with a revised ETA — you don't wait for them to ask.
keyPoints: Personally update the guest with a revised ETA

questions.prompt: Give three situations where a complaint must be escalated to the Duty Manager.
questions.modelAnswer: A refund request or compensation over $50; anything involving safety, security, discrimination or harassment; threats of a public review or legal action or a visibly distressed guest; the same guest complaining a second time during their stay.
keyPoints: Threatens a review or legal action
Second complaint from the same guest
